benchmark_question: Does slop-test-detector make the model better at reviewing test files for weak tests than baseline?
prompt_design: All evals use the same neutral prompt for both with_skill and without_skill conditions. The only variable is whether the skill is available in the execution context (project directory with skills installed vs clean temp directory).

evals.name: empty-and-commented
evals.prompt: Review this test file for weak test patterns and quality issues. For each issue found, report: the pattern name, the test name, the line number, the severity (must-fail vs should-fail), and explain the impact. If the file is clean, say so.
evals.expected_output: Detects empty_test_body and commented_out_assertions as must-fail, plus no_production_call
expectations: Identifies empty test body on 'should process refund for valid transaction'
Identifies empty test body on 'should validate card number format before charging'
Identifies commented-out assertions on 'should validate card number format before charging'
Classifies empty test body and commented-out assertions as must-fail severity
Identifies that 'should log transaction' tests no production code
Does NOT flag 'should reject expired cards' — it has proper assertions and throws
Explains that empty test bodies pass regardless of behavior
Provides line numbers for each finding

forbidden_rules_on_clean_tests: should reject expired cards

evals.name: tautological-circus
evals.prompt: Review this test file for weak test patterns and quality issues. For each issue found, report: the pattern name, the test name, the line number, the severity (must-fail vs should-fail), and explain the impact. If the file is clean, say so.
evals.expected_output: Detects tautological_assertion, conditional_assertion, truthiness_only, and no_production_call
expectations: Identifies tautological assertion on 'should hash password' (assert.ok(true))
Identifies tautological assertion on 'should match known hash' (identical string literals)
Identifies conditional assertion on 'should enforce rate limit' (assertions inside if block)
Classifies tautological and conditional assertions as must-fail
Identifies truthiness-only pattern on 'should hash password'
Does NOT flag 'should generate valid JWT with correct claims' — it has proper value assertions
Explains that assert.ok(true) always passes and verifies nothing
Explains that assertions inside if blocks may never execute

forbidden_rules_on_clean_tests: should generate valid JWT with correct claims

evals.name: truthiness-and-type-only
evals.prompt: Review this test file for weak test patterns and quality issues. For each issue found, report: the pattern name, the test name, the line number, the severity (must-fail vs should-fail), and explain the impact. If the file is clean, say so.
expectations: Identifies typeof-only assertions on 'should detect column types'
Identifies truthiness-only pattern on 'should generate report ID'
Identifies return-value-only check on 'should generate report ID'
Does NOT flag 'should aggregate numeric columns' — it asserts actual values
Explains that typeof-only assertions verify shape but not behavior
Explains that assert.ok(identifier) only checks existence, not correctness
Provides line numbers for each finding

forbidden_rules_on_clean_tests: should aggregate numeric columns with correct totals

evals.name: roundtrip-schema
evals.prompt: Review this test file for weak test patterns and quality issues. For each issue found, report: the pattern name, the test name, the line number, the severity (must-fail vs should-fail), and explain the impact. If the file is clean, say so.
evals.expected_output: Detects literal roundtrip, schema success-only checks, and duplicate assertion sets
expectations: Identifies literal roundtrip on 'should store display name' (asserts same value used in construction)
Identifies literal roundtrip on 'should preserve timezone'
Identifies schema success-only check on 'should validate email format' (only checks .success)
Identifies schema success-only check on 'should accept valid profile'
Identifies duplicate assertion set between the two schema tests
Explains that literal roundtrip tests verify serialization, not logic
Explains that checking only .success misses .data and .error validation
Does NOT report schema success-only on 'should reject profile with missing email' — it checks .error.issues

evals.name: duplicate-no-variation
evals.prompt: Review this test file for weak test patterns and quality issues. For each issue found, report: the pattern name, the test name, the line number, the severity (must-fail vs should-fail), and explain the impact. If the file is clean, say so.
evals.expected_output: Detects duplicate assertion sets and no input variation
expectations: Identifies duplicate assertions between 'should shorten HTTP' and 'should shorten HTTPS'
Identifies duplicate assertions between the two classify tests
Identifies no input variation on classify() — same args in sibling tests
Explains that identical assertion sequences indicate copy-paste without differentiation
Explains that calling the same function with identical args provides no additional coverage
Does NOT flag 'should track click count per slug' — it has unique assertions and inputs

forbidden_rules_on_clean_tests: should track click count per slug

evals.name: no-negative-no-production
evals.prompt: Review this test file for weak test patterns and quality issues. For each issue found, report: the pattern name, the test name, the line number, the severity (must-fail vs should-fail), and explain the impact. If the file is clean, say so.
evals.expected_output: Detects no negative tests and tests that call no production code
expectations: Identifies that the describe block has no negative tests (no throws/rejects)
Identifies that 'should merge default values' calls no production code
Identifies that 'should handle nested keys' calls no production code
Does NOT flag 'should load config from JSON file' — it calls ConfigLoader
Explains that testing only happy paths misses error handling
Explains that tests without production function calls test language guarantees, not app code

should override values from environment variables

evals.name: false-positive-helpers
evals.prompt: Review this test file for weak test patterns and quality issues. The file uses custom assertion helpers (assertEventEmitted, assertPayloadContains, testDeliveryOrder) that internally call assert.*. Take that into account when assessing test quality. Report any issues found.
evals.expected_output: Should recognize assertion equivalents and NOT flag tests as empty or truthiness-only
expectations: Does NOT flag empty test body on any test — assertion equivalents are present
Does NOT flag truthiness-only on any test — helpers count as real assertions
Recognizes that assertEventEmitted, assertPayloadContains, testDeliveryOrder are assertion helpers
If it reports any findings, they are limited to missing negative tests

evals.name: false-positive-conditional
evals.prompt: Review this test file for weak test patterns and quality issues. For each issue found, report: the pattern name, the test name, the line number, the severity (must-fail vs should-fail), and explain the impact. If the file is clean, say so.
evals.expected_output: No findings — conditional setup is different from conditional assertions, and commented code coexists with active assertions
expectations: Reports zero findings or states no issues were detected
Does NOT flag conditional assertion — assertions are AFTER the if block, not inside it
Does NOT flag commented-out assertions — active assertions exist alongside commented ones
Does NOT produce false positives on this tricky file

forbidden_rules_on_clean_tests: should return default value
should evaluate flag based on user segment
should track evaluation metrics
should throw when flag configuration is invalid

evals.name: property-and-vacuous

Explains that fc.property with return true and no assertions passes vacuously
Explains that .length >= 0 is always true and cannot fail
Does NOT flag 'should rank exact matches higher than partial' — proper value assertions
Does NOT flag 'should handle empty query gracefully' — proper value assertion

forbidden_rules_on_clean_tests: should rank exact matches higher than partial

evals.name: defect-comments
evals.prompt: Review this test file for weak test patterns and quality issues. This project enforces a convention where each test must have a preceding '// Defect:' comment explaining what production bug the test catches. Check for missing or trivial defect comments. Report all findings.
evals.expected_output: Detects missing and trivial defect comments
expectations: Identifies missing defect comment on 'should evict least recently used entry'
Identifies missing defect comment on 'should respect max size limit'
Identifies trivial defect comment on 'should handle TTL expiry' ('TTL bug' is too brief)
Does NOT flag 'should update access order' — it has a proper Defect: comment
Explains that Defect: comments must describe what breaks, for whom, and the consequence
Explains that trivial defect comments (too few words) don't convey enough information

forbidden_rules_on_clean_tests: should update access order on get to maintain LRU invariant

evals.name: self-referential

evals.expected_output: Detects self-referential assertions where assert.equal(x, x) compares a variable to itself
expectations: Identifies self-referential assertion on 'should track stock level' (assert.equal(stock, stock))
Identifies self-referential assertion on 'should calculate reorder point' (assert.equal(point, point))
Classifies self-referential assertions as must-fail severity
Explains that assert.equal(x, x) compares a variable to itself and always passes
Does NOT flag 'should deduct stock on order fulfillment' — it asserts against expected value 75
Does NOT flag 'should throw when fulfilling more than available' — proper throws assertion

forbidden_rules_on_clean_tests: should deduct stock on order fulfillment
should throw when fulfilling more than available
